title: Pen N Review
summary: A review of Pen N, a pen I backed on Kickstarter
content:
Back in July I broke my own rule of never backing a hardware Kickstarter and backed a hardware Kickstarter for a Pen N — a pen that supports 100s of refills with a universal clamp that screws into the barrel. I paid $55 for it plus another $20 for shipping.

When it arrived I tried it with a bunch of different refills I had including zento, jetstream, Muji, and they all worked great. No wobbling, exactly as described. It came with a Zebra gel refill which is the one I've kept in it for the past week.

As a pen for grabbing quickly to jot something down, it does the trick but as a pen for writing for long periods of time it's not ideal - this pen is thick. There's no tapering towards the tip so you're just holding a heavy metal sausage[1]. I could only get through the first verse of Michelle Branch's classic "Everywhere" before I stopped filling in the page because it wasn't comfortable.

2026 being the year of pens on carabiners, I opted to pay for the Pen N leather sheath. The pen slips into the sheath, clips in at the top, then can be pulled out the bottom leaving the cap in place near the carabiner hole. Right out the packaging, this was a really tight fit and almost impossible to use but with some finessing and squeezing I was able to loosen the leather up a bit and it works nicely now. This is the spot I like the Pen N the most — as a pen I can clip to my bag and grab it when I need it.

This is a well built pen and the sheath is great but the lack of tapering on the end makes this a pretty uncomfortable pen to use for me so I suspect this is just going to live in my bag or my car for those occasions where I need a pen in a pinch.

  1. Also the name of my Metallica cover band ⤾
